en: A first-class lever like a seesaw multiplies force when the fulcrum is placed closer to the heavy load.
Rough sandpaper creates more friction than smooth glass, slowing down a sliding wooden block much faster.
Earth's gravity pulls a dropped apple downward because the planet's massive mass exerts a continuous attractive force.
An electromagnet magnetizes an iron nail only while electric current flows through the wire coil wrapped around it.
A closed circuit allows electrons to flow from the battery, lighting up the connected bulb instantly.
A glass prism refracts white sunlight into a rainbow because different light colors bend at slightly different angles.
Striking a drum vibrates its tight skin, pushing air molecules to create sound waves that reach our ears.
Heat conducts through a metal spoon in hot soup as fast-moving molecules collide with slower neighboring molecules.
A stretched rubber band stores potential energy that instantly transforms into kinetic energy when released to snap forward.
An inclined plane like a wooden ramp reduces the lifting force needed to roll a heavy box upward.
Two bar magnets repel each other and push apart when their identical north poles are forced close together.
Plucking a tight guitar string makes it vibrate faster than a loose one, producing a higher-pitched sound wave.
